name: WonderSwan
description: Bandai's Japan-only handheld, released in March 1999. Gunpei Yokoi's company Koto Laboratory helped design it, and it ran for around 30 hours on a single AA battery. It could be held horizontally or vertically, and it competed with Nintendo in Japan on price.
curiosities: Gunpei Yokoi, creator of the Game Boy, worked on it but died in 1997, two years before its release.
Many games are designed to be played with the console held vertically.
Gunpey, a puzzle game named after Yokoi, was one of its launch titles.

story: Gunpei Yokoi, who had left Nintendo after creating the Game Boy, designed the WonderSwan for Bandai with his company Koto; it launched in Japan in March 1999, two years after his death.

It was cheap and ran for 30 hours on a single AA battery, and it could be played upright or sideways. Final Fantasy remakes from Square and many anime games kept it alive; a Color model followed in 2000.
It took a share of the Japanese handheld market but never left Japan, and Bandai stopped it in 2003 as the Game Boy Advance spread.
